// why: Compaction is client-side: the gateway never sees it. Starting early
and pruning old tool output is what keeps a turn from growing past the
declared context between two requests, which is the window the server
cannot protect.
skill: a harness that injects every locally-installed skill
description into the system prompt pays for all of them on every
request. Measured on one workstation: 59 skills, 17,754 tokens, 68%
of the session floor. The gateway can refuse such a session and name
the culprit; only the client can stop building it.
todowrite: a task list is paid twice, once as a tool schema on every
request and once as the list itself. The charter already carries the
working discipline.
webfetch/websearch: these route through a third-party API. Off, so the
sovereignty claim stays true at the client as well as the server.
The gateway screens a tool result but cannot shrink it: by the time it
arrives, the tokens are in the request. Native truncation writes the
full output to disk and returns a preview, so nothing is lost.
The gateway refuses dangerous commands, and that refusal cannot be
bypassed. This block is a second, independent barrier for the moments
the gateway is not in the path at all -- a direct model call, an
offline session. Two mechanisms beat one.
